atoms.c: Prenatal testing refers to procedures that determine the sex of an embryo or fetus and test whether it has certain diseases or disabilities before birth.

atoms.b: ... a human in the first eight weeks of development. After the first eight weeks until birth, it is called a fetus.
atoms.c: A human embryo is a human in the first eight weeks of development. After the first eight weeks until birth, it is called a fetus.

atoms.c: Eugenics means the belief that some lives are worth less than others, especially concerning race and disabilities, as well as practices associated with that belief.

instruction.text: Decide whether the arguments are advantages or disadvantages of prenatal testing.
instruction.sound: Decide whether the arguments are advantages or disadvantages of prenatal testing.

atoms.a: If parents know their child will be disabled ahead of time, they will have more time to prepare, both mentally and by providing disability aids or medicine the child might need.
Although this only happens in very rare cases, some forms of prenatal tests risk harming the fetus and increase the possibility of an infection or even miscarriage.
If disabilities are diagnosed prenatally, the chance that the parents opt for an abortion is much higher, fuelling the eugenic view that disabled people do not deserve to live.
In some cultures, sons are valued more than daughters. Female fetuses are aborted much more often than male ones in these countries.

atoms.text: There are many kinds of prenatal tests, some involving genetic testing. These tests only let us know which traits a baby will likely have. However, science may soon take it one step further and allow people to alter a baby's genes before it is born.

b: Prenatal tests can modify an embryo's genes.
All prenatal tests include a gene test.
++Changing an embryo's genes may soon be possible.

atoms.text: Their genetic code could be programmed according to the parents' wishes, from biological sex to eye colour or even certain personality traits. That is why they are referred to as designer babies.

b: Because the procedure is very expensive.
Because they are nothing more than a trend.

atoms.text: If taken even further, these designer babies could be given maximised physical and mental abilities. Their genes could be programmed to make them stronger, faster and more intelligent than regular humans.

instruction.text: Decide whether the arguments are advantages or disadvantages of designer babies.

atoms.a: If addiction or hereditary diseases run in the family, parents can choose better lives for their children by editing out those traits.
Beauty standards and racism are likely to influence parents' choices for their children's physical appearance, leading to less natural diversity.

instruction.text: Decide whether the arguments are advantages or disadvantages of human enhancement.

atoms.a: Humans could be given incredible new abilities and longer life expectancies.
These abilities might cause a social divide between advanced and non-advanced humans and result in discrimination.
